draft.title: Proxy wars
card: A proxy war is a conflict in which two powers support opposing sides, rather than fighting each other directly. The USA and the Soviet Union did this during the Cold War.
They avoided direct war because both had nuclear weapons. A direct clash risked escalating into a nuclear war.
In Korea (1950 to 1953), the Soviet Union and China backed North Korea, while the USA led a United Nations force backing South Korea.

In Vietnam, the USA backed South Vietnam against the communist North, which was supplied by the Soviet Union and China. In Afghanistan (1979 to 1989), Soviet troops fought rebels who received weapons and money from the USA.
draft.remember: Proxy wars let the superpowers compete by backing others, without fighting each other directly.

a.q: Why is the Korean War described as a proxy war?
opts: The superpowers backed opposing sides in Korea
The superpowers declared war on each other
Korea fought as a part of the Soviet Union
Korea was a battle between the USA and China only
a.why: The Soviet Union and China backed North Korea, and the USA backed South Korea, so the rivals competed through others. It was not a war declared between the superpowers themselves.
a.clue: Look at who supported each side.

b.q: Why did the USA and the Soviet Union fight proxy wars rather than attack each other directly?
opts: A direct war risked escalating to nuclear war
Neither superpower had enough soldiers to fight
The United Nations had banned them from fighting
Both superpowers wanted to stay out of other countries
b.why: Both superpowers had nuclear weapons, so a direct clash could have escalated into a nuclear war. Both were in fact heavily involved in other countries, so wanting to stay out is wrong.
b.clue: Think about the weapons both sides held.

a.best: The superpowers backed opposing sides in Korea

b.best: A direct war risked escalating to nuclear war
